text: {"hypotheses":[{"statement":"Introducing a virtual‑memory paging mechanism like MemGPT’s external‑memory/context manager will let the bounded‑memory variant maintain flat recall as the stream grows, because paging can offload older facts while preserving a compact, consolidated memory buffer, thus preventing the accuracy drop seen with naïve append schemes.","confidence":0.78,"support_ids":["a962f389","333b655e","562412ff","ad2ef3b4"],"tags":["memory_management","virtual_paging","bounded_memory","accuracy"]},{"statement":"The abrupt QA accuracy decline after storing more than ~40 items is likely due to token‑budget overflow from naïve appending, which can be mitigated by periodic compression‑based consolidation; such consolidation reduces cross‑fact interference and keeps the active working set within budget, explaining why bounded‑memory approaches avoid the drop.","confidence":0.65,"support_ids":["562412ff","ad2ef3b4","72ccf918","333b655e"],"tags":["token_budget","append_overload","consolidation","accuracy_drop"]}]}
